candidates.title: op_import is a pre-approval full-value EQUALITY ORACLE for any named vault secret (CAPTURE_THE_FLAG included): the import value-reuse classification feeds the broker's pre-approval parse_presets validation, whose client-visible error flips on whether a submitted value equals the stored value
repro_cmds: # All run as the non-root LISTED user redteam, over the live arena socket. One op per connection; the import is withdrawn on disconnect.

# Mechanism: op_import -> broker.request_import() runs import_resolution() then parse_presets(dump_presets(resolution['additions']), vault.names() | resolution['secrets']) BEFORE any approval. A submitted secret whose value != the stored value is RENAMED to NAME_2 and lands in resolution['secrets'] (to_store); a value that EQUALS the stored value is 'unchanged' and NAME_2 is never minted. By pointing a preset at the literal rename target NAME_2, validation passes (PENDING) only when the guess is WRONG, and fails (client error) when the guess is CORRECT.
# (A) the reply a CORRECT guess of CAPTURE_THE_FLAG produces (presets-only is identical to a correct guess: both leave CAPTURE_THE_FLAG_2 unminted):
# ERROR  <=> guess == value(CAPTURE_THE_FLAG) ; PENDING <=> guess != value(CAPTURE_THE_FLAG). Works for any secret name (DATABASE_URL, GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY) by swapping the first arg.
# Deterministic both-legs proof on the REAL broker code against a throwaway vault with a KNOWN flag (open-source code per CHARTER 2; no broker memory/files touched):
candidates.why_novel: Not in README/SECURITY. SECURITY.md 'What counts' puts 'any way for a listed user to read a secret without the console approving it' IN scope; README 'What envh does not do' acknowledges no socket-side value/equality oracle (it states values never leave without approval and the audit log 'holds command lines and reasons, never values'). The import value-reuse feature is described as a user convenience with the classification shown only ON THE CONSOLE before approval. Wave 1 (w1-preset/w1-protocol negatives) explicitly checked this and dismissed it TWICE but missed the join: (1) 'import value-confirmation oracle is NOT exposed ... resolution is never returned to the client before approval' -- true for request.summary, but the resolution ALSO drives the pre-approval parse_presets() call whose ConfigError IS returned to the client; (2) 'preset_validate secret-name oracle is redundant ... reveals nothing new (only the VALUE matters)' -- but here the SAME name-not-in-vault error is made a function of the secret's VALUE via the rename-target reference. Connecting the value-keyed resolution to the client-visible validation error is the novel step.
candidates.notes: Impact: an unapproved, unlimited, per-query 1-bit confidentiality oracle that confirms/denies an exact guess of any named secret's full value, for any listed user, over the socket. It does NOT brute-force the random CTF-FLAG-<hex> sentinel (infeasible), so it is a partial leak (MEDIUM per CHARTER 6), not full exfil -- but it (a) confirms a value learned/suspected via any other channel without touching the console, (b) is a practical dictionary/known-plaintext oracle against low-entropy secret values, and (c) breaches the stated 'no value without approval' boundary. Stealth note: the CORRECT-guess (match) leg raises in request_import BEFORE _announce(), so it writes NO 'request' audit event -- only wrong guesses create+withdraw a request (audit noise); a hit is quieter than a miss. Root cause (src/envh/core/broker.py): request_import() calls import_resolution() (which classifies each submitted value by equality against stored values via `self.vault.get(name) == value` and `value in stored_by_value`, lines 312-338) and then validates the RENAMED additions with parse_presets(..., set(self.vault.names()) | set(resolution['secrets'])) (lines 290-293); the ConfigError is re-raised as RequestError to the client. first_free_name() makes the rename target deterministic (NAME_2), so a crafted preset referencing NAME_2 turns the equality bit into ERROR-vs-PENDING. Fix ideas: run the pre-approval validation against a name set that does not depend on value-equality classification (e.g. validate the SENT presets against vault.names() | set(secrets) regardless of reuse), or defer all import_resolution/validation to approval time. Live broker confirmed healthy after all probes (op_status ok; my import probes withdrew on disconnect, no lingering pending). Supporting scripts left world-readable at /tmp/w2_oneliner.py and /tmp/w2_oracle_localproof.py; full multi-case probe at /tmp/w2_infoleak_probe.py.

negative_results: common.fingerprint() (peek first/last chars + exact length + sha256[:6]) is the single biggest potential leak, but it is reachable ONLY inside request_import()/request summaries and request.result -- i.e. the console view and the post-approval reply. With no approver the socket client never receives request.summary or request.result, so fingerprint/peek/length never reach a non-root client. Re-verified by reading every op reply in server/control.py: pending replies carry only {ok,request_id,pending,notify[,excluded_per_run|presets]}; _reply_decision sends request.result ONLY on outcome=='approved'. Confirms Wave-1 negative.

Timing side channel: import_resolution() uses non-constant-time Python string equality (`self.vault.get(name) == value`) and dict-hash lookup (`value in stored_by_value`) on secret-derived data (unlike the passphrase check, which uses hmac.compare_digest). In principle a prefix-timing oracle, but the comparison is nanoseconds and is fully swamped by asyncio-loop scheduling + socket RTT (ms); not measurably exploitable and not provable per CHARTER 6. Noted as a hardening nit only, NOT claimed. (The equality-oracle finding above is a deterministic error-differential, not a timing one.)

client_connection_lost audit detail = str(ConnectionError/IncompleteReadError) and is written to audit.jsonl (0600 envhsvc) + the console listener; it is NOT returned to the socket client and reading the audit file is out of scope. No client-visible channel.

list_payload / status_payload re-reviewed field-by-field: secrets carry name/approval/max_session/description only; presets carry name/max_session/env(var,secret,approval,in_vault); sessions/runs/pending carry id/vars(names)/pid/uid/reason/command/timestamps. No value bytes, no fingerprint, no length. description is operator-set policy text, not a secret value. Confirms Wave-1.

op_preset_validate returns sorted preset NAMES only; its 'secret X is not in the vault' error is a pure NAME oracle (names already public via op_list) with no value dependence -- distinct from the op_import oracle above, where the same style of error is made value-dependent via the reuse-rename.

No reply field under an unexpected key carries a value for any op/arg combo tried: crafted --with VAR=SECRET and preset mappings only ever surface the SECRET NAME (in list/status/errors), never env_for() output; env_for() values appear only inside _start_run's reply AFTER approval.

import name-agnostic variant (secrets={PROBE:V} with PROBE not in vault, to test 'does V equal ANY stored value' via the `value in stored_by_value` reuse path) cannot be turned into an observable error differential: in both match and no-match the PROBE reference is rewritten through final_names and lands inside the known set, so validation passes either way. The exploitable oracle requires knowing the target secret NAME (which op_list provides), so it is keyed by name as reported.
out_of_scope_observations: The flag value and vault passphrase live only in broker memory / orchestrator context; reading /proc/<pid>/mem or /var/lib/envh-ctf/* would reveal them but is forbidden (CHARTER 3.1/3.2) -- not attempted.

The 0600 audit file (audit.jsonl) contains richer per-event fields (e.g. import_applied added/reused/renamed, secret_revealed) but is unreadable by a non-root user and out of scope to read (CHARTER 3.1).
